Apis India Launches Masala Dates to Target B2C Snacking Market, ETRetail

# Apis India bets on masala dates to expand snacking play, targets B2C growth

 Apis India, a BSE-listed FMCG player, clocking ₹385 crore in trailing twelve-month revenue, is pushing into snacking with a ₹1.5 crore bet on spiced dates, and eyeing a doubling of its B2C business in two years. 

 

- Anurag Sharma
- ETRetail

- Updated On Mar 31, 2026 at 10:38 AM IST

 New Delhi: Apis India is expanding into the packaged snacking segment with the launch of masala dates, as the honey and dates maker looks to accelerate its B2C business and strengthen its presence in general trade and quick commerce, a top official said. The Delhi-headquartered company, which reported ₹385 crore in trailing twelve-month revenue, has invested around ₹1.5 crore to set up a new production line for spiced date snacks at its Roorkee facility, managing director Amit Anand said in an interview with ETRetail. The company has launched masala dates in multiple flavours at a ₹20 price point, targeting impulse snacking and mass distribution across general trade, modern trade and quick commerce platforms. 

### Distribution-led launch strategy

Apis India plans to leverage its existing distribution network for the new product launch. The company currently works with over 500 super stockists, more than 2,000 distributors and around 2.5 lakh retail outlets across India. It is also present in modern trade and quick commerce platforms such as Reliance Retail, Zepto and Blinkit. According to Anand, distribution remains the company’s biggest competitive advantage, especially when launching new products in general trade. 

### Manufacturing expansion and government subsidy

Alongside the new snacking line, Apis India is also expanding its manufacturing capabilities. The company has received ₹1.65 crore subsidy approval from the Ministry of Food Processing Industries under the PMKSY scheme for a fruit and vegetable processing unit in Roorkee. The total project cost for the unit is around ₹4.9 crore, with planned capacity of 2,400 MT per annum. 

The company is also expanding operations in Gujarat and continues to run a manufacturing and distribution setup in Dubai, from where it exports to around 40 countries through B2B channels. 

### Core business and growth focus

While the company is entering snacking, honey continues to remain the core category, with the company reporting 18% volume growth in honey till December 2025 and targeting 25% growth in the category for the full year. Currently, Apis India sources honey from multiple regions including Jammu & Kashmir, Punjab, Haryana, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, Bihar and West Bengal. Apis India further shared that it is targeting doubling its B2C business over the next two years, driven by new product launches, distribution expansion and growing consumption in tier 2 and tier 3 markets.

Detailed Rationale

Crisil Ratings has assigned its ‘ Crisil BBB/ Stable/Crisil A3+’ ratings to the bank facilities of Apis India Limited (AIL; part of Apis group).

The rating reflects a diversified product profile, geographical diversification in revenues backed by the extensive experience of the promoters in the honey business, and healthy financial risk profile. These strengths are partially offset by exposure to intense competition, and working capital intensive operations.

Analytical Approach

Crisil Ratings has combined the business and financial risk profile s of AIL with its wholl y owned subsidiaries of Anantdrishti Smart India Pvt. Ltd. (Incorporated in 2018) and Nature’s Family Tree Foods Pvt. Ltd (Incorporated in 2022) and two associate companies Kapil Anand Agro Pvt. Ltd (50% holding) and APIS Arabia LLC (formerly known as APIS Pure Foodstuff Trading LLC) (49% holding).

Please refer Annexure - List of Entities Consolidated, which captures the list of entities considered and their analytical treatment of consolidation.

Key Rating Drivers - Strengths

- Diversified product profile and geographically diversified revenue backed by e xtensive experience of the promoters: Presence of more than two decades and strong relationships with stakeholders have helped the group to achieve revenue of Rs 349. 7 crore in fiscal 2025. Group is expected to clock revenue of around Rs 4 00 crore in fiscal 2026. Over the years, the group has diversified its product profile by introducing new products such as dates, cornflakes, soya, vermicelli, pickles and jam. This has reduced i ts dependence on honey to around 70-75% in fiscal 2025 from 85% in 2018. The group has also launched flavors and varieties in honey and dates, which will support revenue growth over the medium term. Apis group caters to a wide number of clients, both in India and overseas. The top 10 customers contributed 45-50% of the revenue in fiscal 2025. It consistently derives over 45% of its revenue from exports. Diversity in geographic al reach and clientele should continue to support the group’s business risk profil e.

- Healthy financial risk profile: Networth is strong and projected to be nearly Rs 200 crore for the fiscal ending March 31, 2026 (as against Rs 173 crore as on March 31, 2025). The group’s capital structure has been at healthy level owing to lower reliance on external funds yielding expected gearing and total outside liabilities to adjusted networth (TOL/ANW) ratio of 0.3 time and 0.6 time, respectively, for the fiscal ending March 31, 2026. G earing and TOL/ANW were 0.37 time and 0.66 time, respectively, for the year ending March 31, 2025. The debt protection measures have also been at healthy level due to low leverage and comfortable profitability. The interest coverage and net cash accrual s to adjusted debt (NCA A D) ratio are expected to be 7-8 times and around 0.5 time in fiscal 2026 (6.7 times and 0.5 time for fiscal 2025). The debt protection measures are expected to remain at similar level over medium term.

Key Rating Drivers - We a knesses

- Exposure to intense competition: Low entry barrier has resulted in high fragmentation in the honey market. Food processing industry is highly fragmented in nature due to presence of many unorganised players and organised players in the industry. This restricts pricing flexibility and limits bargaining power with customers and suppliers. 

- Working capital intensive operations: Gross current assets (GCAs) have ranged between 210 and 240 days over the three fiscals ended March 2025 (237 days as on March 31, 2025). Its large working capital requirements arise from its high debtor s (90-120 days) and inventory levels (90-100 days). It is required to extend long credit period. Furthermore, due to its business need, it holds large work in process & inventory. Raw honey is majorly derived from mustard flowers. The procurement for the same has a seaso nality thereby leading to high inventory levels. These are supported by internal accruals, creditor support and working capital limits. GCAs are expected to remain in the range of 230 to 240 days going ahead.

Liquidity Adequate

Bank limi t utilisation is low at around 35 percent for the past twelve months ended November 2025. Net c ash accrual s are expected to be Rs 2 5-3 5 crore annually which will remain more than sufficient against yearly term debt repayment obligation of around Rs 3 crore over the medium term. In addition, it will act as cushion to the liquidity. Current ratio was healthy at 2.13 times on March 31, 2025 and projected at a similar level for fiscal ending March 31, 2026. Low gearing and strong networth support the financial flexibility and provide the financial cushion available in case of any adverse conditions or downturn in the business. 

Outlook Stable

Crisil Ratings believes that Apis group will continue to benefit from the extensive experience of its promoters, and established relationships with clients. 

Upward factors 

- Sustained improvement in scale of operation s by around 20% and sustenance of operating margin at around 10% leading to higher net cash accruals.
- Efficient management of working capital cycle and sustenance of financial risk profile

Downward factors

- Decline in revenue or a d ecline in operating margins below 6% leading to lower net cash accruals.
- Large debt-funded capital expenditure or stretch in the working capital cycle weaken ing the capital structure and liquidity

About the Group

AIL was setup in 1924 and acquired by the late Mr Deepak Anand and his family member in 2006. The company is currently headed by Mr. Deepak’s sons, Mr Amit Anand and Mr Vimal Anand. AIL processes honey for domestic and global markets. It has also expanded in the B2C market and has introduced products such as dates, ginger garlic paste, pickles and jam. The company markets its products under the brand name “Apis”. The company’s manufacturing unit is located in Roorkee (Uttarakhand). Addition ally, it has an overseas manufacturing facility in Dubai (UAE). AIL’s equity shares are listed on BSE Limited. 

AIL has two wholly owned subsidiaries- Anantdrishti Smart India Pvt. Ltd. (Incorporated in 2018) and Nature’s Family Tree Foods Pvt. Ltd (Incorporated in 2022) and two associate companies Kapil Anand Agro Pvt. Ltd (50% holding) and APIS Arabia LLC (formerly known as APIS Pure Foodstuff Trading LLC) (49% holding).

Details of instruments/facilities in Annexure-1.

Rationale and key rating drivers Reaffirmation in ratings assigned to bank facilities of Apis India Limited (AIL) derives strength from its experienced promoters with established track record of operations in honey, diversified product profile and established brand name of “Apis”. Ratings also take comfort from the healthy financial risk characterised by comfortable overall gearing and improving debt coverage indicators. However, ratings are constrained by working capital intensive operations, margin susceptible to raw material prices and competition from organised and unorganised players. Ratings also take note of delays in the realisation of export proceeds from its overseas customers, for which company has filed an appeal for review, which is key monitorable.

Rating sensitivities: Factors likely to lead to rating actions

Positive factors

• Growth in scale of operations as marked by the total operating income (TOI) above ₹400 crore and Profit before interest, lease, depreciation, and tax (PBILDT) margins above 11.00% on a sustained basis. 
• Efficient management of working capital cycle and resultant improvement in liquidity position. 

Negative factors

• Decline in scale of operations by over 20% from current levels and/or reduction in PBILDT margin below 6.00% on a sustained basis. 
• Sizeable capex undertaken by the company adversely, impacting the capital structure with the overall gearing exceeding 1.00x. 
• Collection/inventory period moderating, leading to working capital cycle above 180 days and weakening liquidity position of the company. 
Analytical approach: Consolidated 
Consolidated approach with two wholly owned subsidiaries: Anantadrishti Smart India Private Limited and Nature’s Family Tree 
Foods Private Limited and two associate companies Kapil Anand Agro Private Limited (KAAPL; 50% shareholding) and APIS Pure 
Foodstuff Trading LLC (APFTL; 49% shareholding). Subsidiaries/Associates considered for consolidated financial statements for 
FY25 are listed under Annexure-6. 
Outlook: Stable 
The stable outlook reflects CARE Ratings Limited’s (CareEdge Ratings) opinion that the company will continue to benefit from its 
experienced promoters with established track record and diversified product profile. 

Detailed description of key rating drivers:

Key strengths 
Experienced promoters with established track record of operations 
AIL’s operations are overseen by Amit Anand and Vimal Anand. The company’s current manufacturing facility in Roorkee, 
Uttarakhand was established in 2012 under the leadership of their father, late Deepak Anand. Prior to this, the group operated a 
honey processing unit in Rajpura, Punjab, which was subsequently discontinued. 

1Complete definition of ratings assigned are available at www.careratings.com and other CARE Ratings Limited’s publications.

Promoters bring over a decade of experience in the food processing industry and are supported by a team of professionals with diverse expertise across functional areas. Their long-standing presence in the sector has enabled development of enduring relationships with clients and suppliers. AIL markets its products under its proprietary brand “Apis,” which enjoys strong brand recognition and customer acceptance across India.

Healthy Financial risk profile 
AIL continues to maintain a strong financial position, supported by steady growth in revenue and improved profitability. In FY25 
(refers to April 01 to March 31), the company recorded an operating income of ₹350.35 crore (PY: ₹317.20). Despite this growth, 
the company’s PBILDT margin saw a slight dip to 10.18% in FY25 from 11.18% in FY24. Moderation in margin was primarily due 
to higher input costs and subdued export demand to the USA. The company’s net worth improved to ₹172.99 crore (PY: ₹147.77 
crore) including investment in associate companies of ₹39.88 crore (PY: ₹35.51 crore) in FY25. 

While domestic demand remained resilient, supported by rising health consciousness and a consumer shift toward natural sweeteners, the export performance was constrained following introduction of a minimum export price (MEP) in 2024. This regulatory change put pressure on export volumes and pricing, impacting global competitiveness of Indian honey processors. However, the company’s presence across diversified product segments such as dates, jam, pickles, and ginger-garlic paste among other food products has helped cushion the impact of weak export performance, although these segments generally yield lower margins compared to its core honey business.

Despite the slight dip in profitability margins, the company’s capital structure remains healthy. The company’s overall gearing improved to 0.38x in FY25 from 0.41x in FY24, while interest coverage also increased to 7.11x in FY25 from 5.99x in FY24, reflecting improved debt servicing capacity. Given its healthy cash flows, diversified product mix, and prudent financial management, AIL is well-positioned to manage ongoing challenges in the honey processing sector and maintain financial stability going forward.

Key weaknesses 
Elongated Operating cycle 
Raw honey, which constitutes the core product of AIL, is predominantly sourced from mustard flowers. Procurement of this raw 
material follows a seasonal pattern, with bulk of sourcing occurring between October and March each year. As a result, the 
company typically experiences significant inventory buildup towards the end of the fiscal year, contributing to elevated inventory 
holding levels. In FY25, the company reported an operating cycle of 177 days in compared to 159 days in the previous year, 
primarily driven by increase in receivable days from 93 days in FY24 to 103 days in FY25, decrease in creditors days from 53 days 
in FY24 to 40 days in FY25 and high inventory of 113 days (PY: 119 days) in FY25. Given the seasonal nature of procurement 
and inventory-intensive nature of honey processing, the operating cycle is expected to remain within a similar range going forward. 

Susceptibility of fluctuations in raw material prices and seasonal nature of operations Adverse climatic conditions may affect availability of raw material and lead to volatility in the prices. The behaviour and life cycle of honeybees depends completely on climatic and floristic conditions, that is, flowering of plants, secretion of nectar and production of pollen, which may vary from place to place. Moreover, raw honey is majorly derived from the mustard flowers. The procurement for the same has a seasonality where most of the procurement is done in the January to June period every year. Consumption of honey is also the highest in the winter months in Q3 (October to December) and Q4 (January to March) of the financial year, which slightly concentrates sales (especially domestic sales) to this part of the year. AIL procures raw honey from bee farmers through its collection representatives and agents across the country. Dates are mostly imported from Gulf countries, with sorting and packaging done at the facility in Roorkee. Other products under the “Apis” brand name are manufactured or processed on job work basis by vendors.

Highly fragmented and competitive industry The honey and other food processing industry is highly fragmented in nature due to presence of a large number of unorganised players and organised players in the industry. The competition restricts pricing flexibility and limits bargaining power with customers and suppliers. As such good customer relation and quality maintenance are significantly important for business growth. Moreover, business is also susceptible to changing preferences of consumers towards flavours and brands.

Liquidity: Adequate AIL’s liquidity position is adequate, supported by an expected gross cash accrual (GCA) of ~₹32 crore in FY26 against scheduled debt repayment obligations of ₹3.72 crore. The average utilisation levels ~76.73% for 12 months ended in May 2025, providing

cushion to its fund requirements. As of March 31, 2025, the company reported a current ratio of 2.14x, indicating a healthy short term liquidity buffer.

The company does not have major debt-funded capital expenditure plans in the near-to-medium term, apart from a planned investment of ₹4–5 crore for establishing a jam processing unit and a dates factory. This will be funded through mix of government subsidy, term loan and internal accruals.

Apis India’s FMCG pivot: Repositioning for the wellness economy

# Apis India’s FMCG pivot: Repositioning for the wellness economy 

 Sallavi Gowda | 7 months ago Views: 1274 Add Adgully as preferred on 

As India’s FMCG landscape undergoes a decisive shift toward clean-label, functional nutrition, legacy players are being forced to rethink both portfolio and positioning. Once known primarily as one of the country’s largest organised honey exporters, Apis India is now actively transitioning into a broader wellness-focused brand, tapping into the fast-growing intersection of health, convenience, and everyday consumption.

The company’s evolution – from a single-category export-driven business to a diversified player spanning dates, saffron, jams, and now healthy snacking – reflects a larger industry pivot. Rising consumer awareness, post-pandemic health consciousness, and the demand for accessible “better-for-you” products are reshaping how FMCG brands innovate and compete.

In this context, Apis India’s latest push into healthy snacking with products like masala-coated dates signals a strategic attempt to move beyond commoditised categories and create new consumption occasions. 

In conversation with Adgully, Amit Anand, Managing Director, Apis India, outlines how the brand is leveraging its legacy in sourcing and quality while adapting to changing consumer behaviour, increasing competition from new-age wellness brands, and the growing importance of convenience-led nutrition. 

Apis India has long been known as one of the country’s largest organised honey exporters. How has the brand evolved over the years from being a honey-focused company to building a broader clean-nutrition portfolio? 

We were always a honey company, but when we entered the B2C FMCG space, we needed a wider product portfolio. That’s when we expanded into categories aligned with wellness. We introduced dates, leveraging our Middle East connections, and built a strong presence there.

From there, we moved into adjacent categories like jams and other wellness products such as saffron. Over time, we have built a diverse portfolio centred around health and wellness, allowing us to cater to evolving consumer demand. 

What gap in consumer behaviour or demand are you aiming to address with the launch of a new product in the clean-nutrition space? 

Post-COVID, consumers have become far more health-conscious, especially in snacking. We saw an opportunity to create a product that is both healthy and aligned with Indian taste preferences.

Our new offering, masala-coated dates, is designed as a healthy snacking option. The idea is similar to how makhana gained popularity. We believe dates can emerge as a strong alternative in the healthy snack category, which is growing rapidly. 

Consumers today are far more conscious about what goes into their food, especially in categories like honey and natural products. How is Apis India building trust and transparency around sourcing and quality? 

For us, quality is everything. Every batch of honey that comes into our factory is tested, and every box of dates undergoes strict quality checks.

We have a strong in-house lab and dedicated teams to ensure that only the best quality products reach consumers. Our growth over the years has been driven by this consistent focus on quality and trust. 

The FMCG space has become extremely competitive, with both legacy players and new-age health brands entering the market. How does Apis India stay relevant in such a crowded landscape? 

Our foundation is quality and legacy. We have been in the honey business since 1991 and have a deep understanding of consumer preferences.

At the same time, we focus on offering high-quality products at affordable prices. Innovation also plays a key role. With products like masala dates, we are trying to create new spaces within the category rather than just compete in existing ones. 

There’s clearly growing interest in natural, functional and clean-label foods. From your perspective, how big is this shift and what does it mean for the future of the FMCG sector in India? 

This shift is very strong and will continue to grow. As incomes rise and awareness increases, consumers are moving towards healthier and wellness-oriented products.

FMCG as a sector will always grow, but within that, health and wellness products will see even faster growth in the coming years. 

Apis India has a strong export presence as well. Do global consumer trends influence the kind of products you develop for the Indian market? 

Yes, absolutely. Being present globally gives us a strong perspective on emerging trends. We observe what works in developed markets and use those insights.

However, India is a unique market, so we always adapt our products to suit local tastes and preferences. 

Ready-to-eat and convenience foods are becoming more popular, especially in urban markets. How do you balance convenience with the brand’s focus on natural and healthy products? 

Convenience is becoming very important as lifestyles change and more people are working. Consumers are looking for products that are easy to consume without compromising on health.

That’s where ready-to-eat healthy snacks come in. Products like our masala dates offer both convenience and nutrition, making them relevant for today’s consumers. 

Looking ahead, what are the key growth areas for Apis India over the next few years in terms of product innovation and market expansion? 

We are targeting steady growth and see healthy snacking as a key opportunity area. Entering this category will help us expand further and reach new consumers.

If the response to our new products continues to be positive, we believe it will significantly contribute to our growth in the coming years.

## QUARTERLY PERFORMANCE

Management Commentary “We reported revenue of Rs. 17,986 Lacs in H1FY27 mainly supported by sustained demand. Dates have shown healthy growth. On the distribution front, General Trade delivered a healthy performance during H1FY27, reflecting continued market traction and the effectiveness of our distribution network. With a 55% YoY growth, the EBITDA was booked at Rs. 1,831 Lacs translating into 10% margin. Calibrated pricing actions during the period helped mitigate the impact of elevated raw material costs and packaging costs. our focus on operational efficiencies helped us navigate the overall cost pressures effectively. The demand remained resilient, reflecting strong customer preference for our products and the strength of our brand. In H1FY27, we brought the production and packing of jam products under our own manufacturing operations, which were previously outsourced to a third party. This transition is expected to provide greater control over the manufacturing process, improve cost efficiencies and strengthen our pricing competitiveness. Going forward, we intend to leverage these advantages to significantly expand the category, with an ambition to grow jam sales by 10x over the coming period Talking about our international presence, Apis Arabia Foods LLC, Dubai, our overseas associate company, helps us establish our presence in the Middle East for trade operations in the geography for honey, tea, coffee and bread and bakery products. We remain optimistic on its contribution to the overall business. Going forward, we will remain focused on strengthening our market presence, expanding consumer reach and sustaining a balanced approach towards growth and profitability.”

MR. VIMAL ANAND Whole-time Director, Apis India Limited
